w: The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, London is as the ancient scriptures prescribe. Perfect in every sense, a house fit for God. It is no wonder that thousands of Hindus and non-Hindus alike are drawn to the mandir as a bee is inevitably drawn to a blossoming garden.
The Murti-Pratishtha Ceremony With all preparations complete, the day of the murti-pratishtha ceremony arrived – Sunday 20 August 1995, Shravan Vad 10 of the Indian year Vikram Samvat 2051.

The scriptures implicitly say that whilst it is important that the murtis be consecrated by performing the correct rituals, it is more important that they are consecrated by a person who is himself the receptacle for God's unlimited grace. Such a God-realized Sadhu is to be asked to perform the rituals, and it is when he asks God to enter the murtis and specially become accessible that God cannot refuse.

At 9.00am, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj arrived in the Mandir, he was greated by BAPS Swaminarayan Youth band from Leicester, UK, Dallas, USA and Nairobi, Kenya played auspicious tune. Swamishri began walking up to the mandir on the red carpet, having sent his beloved Harikrishna Maharaj ahead. As usual, he was carried up the mandir steps in a special chair but asked to be put down for the final 10 steps. From there, he climbed unaided to approach the first two pillars that support the entrance arch. A string of balloons had been hung above the arch. On the press of a button, they burst to release thousands of petals that floated down to shower Swamishri in welcome.

The rituals were being performed under the main dome. A special seat had been prepared for Swamishri, and around him sat some 250 well-wishers and senior devotees. For lack of space, only they were allowed to eye witness the historic events unfolding before them. The several thousand other guests and devotees were attentively watching the proceedings live on giant video screens in the marquee. Millions of Europeans were also brought into the mandir by Zee TV which was broadcasting the entire ceremony live.

Behind Swamishri sat the special guests. Leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party of India – Mr. Advani, the High Commissioner for India – Dr. L.M. Singhvi, the Chief Ministers of Gujarat and Rajasthan States – Keshubhai Patel and Bhairon Singh Shekhawat respectively.

Swamishri himself began to perform the prescribed rituals as Brahmins chanted the appropriate Vedic hymns and verses. The chanting and prayers reverberated around the dome, charging the atmosphere with divinity.

Finally, at 9.38am, Swamishri was asked to enter the sanctum sanctorum and begin the final rituals and prayers that would perfectly consecrate the murtis. Whilst he himself performed the basic pratishtha rituals on the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami and Gopalanand Swami in the central sanctum, he asked Pujya Mahant Swami to do similar with Harikrishna Maharaj and Radha Krishna on the left, and Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami to do likewise with Ghanshyam Maharaj on the right. In the outer sanctums, he asked other senior sadhus to perform the rituals for the murtis of Shiva-Parvati, Ram-Sita, Hanumanji and Ganesh, and the marble murtis of the Guru Parampara placed behind the main sanctum. Swamishri also performed the final rituals for the other murtis in the inner sanctum.

After the ceremonies, the curtain to the sanctum was closed and as everyone waited outside, the murtis were clothed in regal splendor and an annakut of hundreds of vegetarian dishes placed artistically before them. This was the first offering.

At 10.13am the curtains were drawn open to reveal the deities, now fully consecrated in all their royal divinity. Swamishri, the sadhus and other guests were given lighted wicks with which to perform the arti – that would announce to the world the completion of the Vedic ceremonies. The mandir, now no longer just a beautiful inert physical object, but new radiated with the infinite divinity and tranquility of God.
Swamishri and the guests were then led downstairs into the exhibition, 'Understanding Hinduism'. This permanent exhibition introduces people to the basic beliefs and traditions of Hinduism.

Next, the group walked across the mandir compound to the Haveli. Swamishri asked Chandubhai Dalia to declare it open. Returning to their awaiting cars, the group was led to a giant cloud of orange balloons. Swamishri released them. At the same instance from behind the mandir, were released 7500 orange balloons that shot up into the sky signalling the celebration of the murti pratistha of the mandir.
Swamishri arrived at Philadelphia at 10.10 am. On reaching the mandir, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha ceremony. More than 2,500 devotees and well-wishers attended the occasion.

Swamishri sanctified the 'Pramukh Swami Institute of Information Technology' at the Akshar Purushottam Chhatralay campus. Swamishri also inspired the youths to excel academically as well as integrate moral and spiritual virtues in their lives.

The Janmashtami celebration commenced at 9.00 p.m. Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami addressed the assembly and thereafter kishores performed a cultural dance. Pujya Viveksagar Swami explained the significance of festivals and thereafter Pujya Mahant Swami addressed the assembly. Kirtans and another cultural dance gave the celebration a devotional and festive flair. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, "On festival days one should sing God's glory, remember Him and live a life that pleases Him. We have to imbibe the knowledge He has imparted and the moral injuctions He has prescribed. God comes on earth to redeem us, therefore we should internalize virtues to please Him. "Many people gamble on this festive day. But that does not please God. However people have tendencies to celebrate festivals by gambling, partying and enjoying themselves in mundane ways...

"God has said in the Gita that there are two types of people: good and evil. When evil increases, God Himself takes birth on earth to destroy it and establish dharma and spiritual values. He transforms a person into a real man and redeems him... God does not like ego. So to please God first, one must give up one's tendency of possessiveness and humbly offer devotion to Him..."
During the evening satsang assembly the murti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was honoured by the devotees of Bangalore.

Today after the midday meal, Mahant Swami Maharaj was going to his residence, meeting the devotees through his glance. At that time Shyamalbhai of Ahmedabad was standing with his little son Jitendra. Whenever Swamishri sees a child, he always stops, puts his hand on the child's head, shows affection and gives blessings. The same happened here too.

But as soon as Swamishri put his hand on Jitendra's head, Jitendra at once stretched out his little hand to put it on Swamishri's head. Seeing this, his father immediately pulled back the child's outstretched hand. But Swamishri, laughing, stood still to let him put his hand there and said, "Put it... put it..."
All who saw this were charmed by Swamishri, "humble and very wise..."

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj left by car for the airport to go to Dallas. Vikasbhai Desai of Digas was doing the seva of driving. When talk turned to him, Swamishri showed with his hand where his house is and how it is located. When asked, Vikasbhai said, "Swamishri came to my home in 2010!"
After seven years, who would remember whose house it is and how it is located?! And that too after thousands of such visits to homes?! There is no match for Swamishri's power of memory.

ds.p: On the flight from Houston to Dallas
w: Shri Prashantbhai Mehta, the owner of the aircraft, was sitting beside Mahant Swami Maharaj. Prashantbhai asked Swamishri openly, "What should I do to get rid of ego?"
"If one understands the true glory of Bhagwan's form, ego goes away," Swamishri told him.
Mahant Swami Maharaj had arrived at the assembly venue, the Verizon Theatre, at 6.00. But he was to enter the assembly at a particular time, and there was still time before that.

Making good use of the time, personal meetings were arranged with the dignitaries who would be on stage. Among them, Texas Congressman Shri Pete Sessions met Swamishri and said, "Your presence is very important." Saying this, he also began to put forward his family's problems: he has two sons. As he spoke about one who has a physical problem, he became a little emotional.

Swamishri immediately looked at the attendant sadhu and said, "Tissue." No one knew why Swamishri was asking for a tissue. Still, a tissue was quickly given to Swamishri, and Swamishri gave the tissue to Shri Pete Sessions, because Swamishri had seen that the corners of his eyes had become wet. He truly felt very good. He said, "I felt great joy. From here I have received faith to live."
After Mahant Swami Maharaj sang the chesta, Viveksagardas Swami phoned. He said to Swamishri, "The parayans (scripture reading series) of the month of Shravan are over, so please give a message."

Swamishri said, "The same message: glory. That is, Shriji Maharaj is the highest of the high. Everything else is the countless universes, but no one can go beyond the universes. Only Shriji Maharaj, Swami and the muktas can. And apart from Shriji Maharaj and Swami, there is no moksha at all."
